why: A class folder holds its class's methods (MATLAB doc 'Class Folders', 'Methods in Separate Files'). A classdef class's methods are those of its own folder: `extra/@crate/fluff.m` is no method of the class `lib/@crate/crate.m`, so `fluff(c)` reaches nothing and stays a live row. An old-style class's methods are the functions of every `@plume` folder on the path (the legacy class model, which built-in types' class folders such as `@double` still follow; project rule since step 15), so `fluff(p)` on a `plume` calls `extra/@plume/fluff.m`, a folder that holds no constructor of its own.
